execution.description: Battery's Level 0 attack adapter (slice AT-B of OWNER-GRAPHITE-ATTACKER-01). It runs the eight Track A checks as nine families and two seams, against the real boundaries, with specimens, trained and held-out controls and twelve mutations.

expected: track_a's five families could be reused unchanged and the remaining checks added beside them, with every name an agent might see passing Graphite's protected-material check.
observed: Graphite's protected-material check refused more than expected. The Track A check id fresh_attack_confirmation contains the deny fragment 'confirmation'. Every control named after the EV4 panel contains 'ev4'. track_a's canary needles contain 'canary'. The first draft reported a staged-canary leak as an exposure (OTHER_SIGNAL) instead of a breach (FAILING_TRIGGER), because the output scan ran before the detector. A cold `import carbon.agent_campaign.graphite.tools` fails on its circular import with `literature` unless `literature` loads first. `climb.ClimbPlan` refuses level 0, so a Level 0 ablation has to reuse the registered Level 1 draft plan, whose previous and ablated profiles are both Level 0. An accepted battery compile costs about 0.45 s. A contract-level refusal is near-instant, so a sweep over all 40 withheld capabilities costs little, and the panel controls dominate the run time.
keep: Look up a reused harness's boundaries at call time, so that a weakened boundary is seen and the harness's own report stays byte-identical.
Decide a breach before scanning a boundary's output for protected text, and keep evidence only by digest.
Derive permission sweeps from the live contract, read only, rather than from a hand-written list.
change: Check every agent-visible name against agent_campaign.boundaries.DENY_FRAGMENTS when it is written: check ids such as fresh_attack_confirmation, and anything named after EV4 or EV5, are Carbon's vocabulary only.
Make graphite.tools importable on its own, or document that literature loads first.
protocol_elements: the eight shared Track A checks, each with an attack example and a valid control
trained and held-out controls, with the held-out controls read only for the wrongful-rejection rate
